_comment: The demo's entire Nextcloud, as one file. `npm run demo` serves it through
test/mock-nextcloud/ and boots the real app against it.
Files: a folder has `children`; a file has `text` (typed inline) or `asset`
(a real file, path relative to this JSON file). `contentType` is guessed
from the extension unless you say otherwise.
sharedBy: only on a top-level file/folder -- marks it as something the
named person actually shared with the viewer account. The home page only
shows entries carrying it. Documents/Photos/Templates/etc below have no
sharedBy on purpose: that is the skeleton content a fresh Nextcloud account
seeds itself with, and the whole point of this dataset entry is to prove
the app hides it.
Dates: absolute ("2026-08-12", or a full ISO timestamp) or an offset from
now -- "-3h", "+2d", "-45m". Offsets are what keep this file believable a
year from now, so the recently-touched files below stay recent and no task
is permanently overdue. The Latest page groups them by day, so the offsets
are spread on purpose: a couple within today, a couple yesterday, then a
trail back through last week.
Tasks: each list has a displayName, an optional #rrggbb colour, and tasks
with summary / description / due / status / completed / percent / priority /
subtasks. `completed` implies the task is done.
Edit anything here and re-run `npm run demo`. Nothing else needs changing.
